peoples.name: the folk of {S}
peoples.history: their grandparents' grandparents were Caldor's river tribes, and they stayed when the kingdom fell.

boon.text: carts of grain and cheese come up the road from {S}

peoples.name: the halflings of {S}
peoples.history: they settled the farms the Crown Marches emptied, and they remember who fed them in the Red Tide.

boon.text: barrels of {S} brown ale roll into the taverns

peoples.name: the dwarves of {S}
peoples.history: they are heirs of Khaz Varrund, the Deep Realm, and they have never forgiven the dragons.

boon.text: dwarven smiths of {S} send tools and iron to the market

peoples.name: the elves of {S}
peoples.history: they are the last of the Court of First Leaves, and they remember Caldor's axes. They live in the canopy now, in pod-halls strung between the great trees by rope walks, and come down only when they choose.

boon.text: the elves of {S} mark which trees may be felled, and their guides walk the town's companies through the deep wood by paths only they know

peoples.name: the gnomes of {S}
peoples.history: they stayed in Khaz Varrund's lower workings when the dwarves fled, and have mapped every tunnel since.

boon.text: gnome tinkers from {S} trade clockwork and maps of the deep ways

peoples.name: the lizardfolk of {S}
peoples.history: they served the serpent-priests of the Coil and outlived them, and they will not go to the Drowned Temple.

boon.text: lizardfolk guides from {S} trade eels and show safe paths through the fen

peoples.name: the brothers and sisters of {S}
peoples.history: their order was founded by the Dawn Wardens who held the Dawn Gate through the first Long Night.

peoples.name: the merchant captains of {S}
peoples.history: their harbour shut its gates on the Long Night and opened them as a free city, and it has knelt to no crown since.

boon.text: ships from {S} bring wine, salt fish and sellswords

peoples.name: the frost-sworn of {S}
peoples.history: their jarls sent three of Caldor's armies home in boxes, and they despise tribute.

boon.text: the frost-sworn of {S} send furs, smoked meat and young warriors

peoples.name: the caravan lords of {S}
peoples.history: they are the grandchildren of the Ninefold Throne of Ashkaar, and they know which tombs to leave shut.

boon.text: caravans from {S} unload spice, silk and date wine

themes.name: farmland
themes.text: hedged fields and quiet mills, with trouble on the roads
history: In the Age of Crowns these fields fed Caldor. The Red Tide burned them in 380 AL, and halflings settled the empty farms after.
Caldor's tax roads still run straight as a spear under the hedges here, though the milestones have been carted off for walls.
Every barrow in these downs is older than the farms. The farmers plough round them and do not ask whose they are.

wander: something has been taking sheep from the far pasture
raiders lying in wait by the hedgerow
a fight in a burned-out barn
trap: a snare pit dug across the cart track
a rigged hayloft
hazard: the ford runs high after the rains
a grass fire driven by the wind
puzzle: a miller's ledger written in a private cipher
parley: a frightened shepherd who saw where they went
a reeve who knows the back ways
treasure: a strongbox buried under the threshing floor
the raiders' stash in a hollow oak
boss: the one who leads them, waiting in the loft
their chief, counting stolen coin

themes.name: deep forest
themes.text: giant trees, bramble walls and mossy stone circles
history: These woods belonged to the Court of First Leaves before any human cut a tree, and the elves remember every axe.
The stone circles in this wood were raised by the Court of First Leaves to mark bargains with the Green Hush. Some of the bargains have not ended.
Caldor's foresters cut a road through here in the Age of Crowns. The wood took it back in a single lifetime.

wander: something else is hunting in the wood
eyes in the undergrowth
the trees go quiet around them
trap: a deadfall strung between two trunks
a ring of mushrooms that should not be stepped in
hazard: the trail vanishes into briar and bog
a fog that turns them in circles
puzzle: a standing stone that asks a riddle in a rustle of leaves
a sealed door in the roots of a great oak
parley: a hermit who knows where the lair lies
an elf scout watching from the branches
treasure: offerings left at a moss-grown shrine
a ranger's lost cache
boss: the master of the wood's dark heart
the thing in the hollow tree

themes.name: mountains
themes.text: scree slopes, pine ridges and high passes riddled with old mine adits
history: The Stonekings cut their halls into these peaks before Vermithrax burned them out, and the Red Tide came down these same passes in 380 AL.
The mine adits in these crags were dug by the Smith-King's holds, who guarded the passes for three thousand years.
Giant-sized stairs climb these slopes to nowhere: the last of a Stoneking hall that Vermithrax burned off the mountain.

wander: something comes down the pass at dusk
tracks too big for any goat
shapes on the ridge above
trap: a dwarf rune-trap still primed in the old tunnel
a rockfall rigged above the path
hazard: a narrow ledge over a thousand-foot drop
a sudden blizzard on the pass
bad air in the lower shafts
puzzle: a dwarf vault-door locked by a sequence of runes
a mine cart rail that switches by the old guild's code
parley: a goat-herd who knows the hidden pass
a dwarf prospector who wants an escort
treasure: a forgotten ore cart full of silver
a dwarf lord's tomb-hoard
boss: whatever took the deepest hall
the master of the drowned forge

themes.name: caverns
themes.text: cave mouths that breathe cold air, and dungeons going down and down
history: These are the upper workings of Khaz Varrund, the dwarves' Deep Realm, abandoned when its miners broke into something below that breathed.
The deep gnomes say the dwarves who dug here fled in a single night, and left their suppers on the tables.
Somewhere below these caves is the breach where Khaz Varrund's miners broke through. The air still comes up from it, warm.

wander: something stirs in the dark
a skittering in the side passage
lights where no lights should be
trap: a tripwire strung across the passage
a pressure plate under the dust
a false floor over a spiked pit
hazard: a flooded crawlway
a chasm crossed by a rotten rope bridge
puzzle: a sealed door that answers in riddles
a lever room where only one combination is safe
parley: a lost deep gnome who will trade directions for food
a prisoner chained in a side cell
treasure: a chest in a forgotten alcove
the hoard heaped in the lowest cavern
boss: the master of the deep halls
the thing at the bottom of the stair

themes.name: castle ruins
themes.text: toppled castles and broken highways of a kingdom that fell
history: This was the heartland of the High Kingdom of Caldor, which ruled from the coast to the sands until the first Long Night.
Caldor's lords fought over these castles for seven centuries after the kingdom fell, and every one of them claimed the crown.
These walls were built in Ostrava's name, and her law is still carved on the gateposts, if anyone could read it.

names: the Vault of the Last King

wander: squatters in the ruined outbuildings
lookouts on the broken wall
something nesting in the chapel
trap: a rotten stair rigged to collapse
a portcullis that drops behind them
hazard: a collapsing curtain wall
a flooded undercroft
puzzle: the old king's seal-lock on the treasury
a library whose shelves hide a door
parley: a deserter who wants out
a ghost of a castellan who wants a debt paid
treasure: the toll-chest in the guardroom
a royal strongroom nobody found
boss: whatever sits the broken throne now
the thing that rules the keep now

themes.name: haunted moor
themes.text: heath, standing stones and mass graves where the dead walk
history: Caldor's civil wars filled this moor with mass graves, and in the first Long Night its dead were the first to walk.
The Field of Spears was fought here in 140 BL, and the grass still grows thin over the grave pits.
The Dawn Wardens held a gate on this heath through the whole of the first Long Night, until the Lantern Mother lit her lamp.

wander: the barrow-mist rises and something walks in it
dead hands push up through the turf
trap: a tomb-guardian's spear-trap
a sarcophagus lid that slams on grasping hands
hazard: a grave-chill that saps the strength
a sinkhole into an older barrow
puzzle: a burial riddle carved on the lintel
a ring of bells that must be rung in order
parley: a gravekeeper who knows the old names
a restless ghost who bargains for rest
treasure: grave goods of a forgotten king
a reliquary of tarnished silver
boss: whatever sleeps on the barrow-king's bier
the keeper of the ossuary

themes.name: swamp
themes.text: reed beds, stilt villages and sinking ruins lost in fog
history: Before the sea rose the serpent-priests of the Coil ruled here. Their temples sank with their saints still inside.
The lizardfolk say the Coil's saints are not dead in their sunken temples, only waiting for the water to go down.
Before the Coil drowned, the river tribes paid its tithe in eels at the edge of this marsh.

wander: the marsh is not empty
something big slides off a mudbank
lights bobbing over the water
trap: a sunken stake-line under the black water
a hag's ward woven of hair and bone
hazard: flooded halls where the air runs out
sucking mud to the waist
leech-thick water
puzzle: a sealed reliquary that answers in riddles
a drowned altar with a tide-lock
parley: a lizardfolk hunter who will guide for meat
a marsh witch who trades in favours
treasure: an altar heaped with offerings
a sunken barge's strongbox
boss: the thing beneath the drowned bell
whatever lives in the island hut

themes.name: coast
themes.text: cliffs, coves and reefs where smugglers and worse come ashore
history: These were Caldor's harbours, free cities since the Fall, and their wharves bred the Gilded Scale and the Quiet Hand.
Caldor's treasure fleets sailed from these coves, and some of them are still on the reefs.
The Quiet Hand was born on these wharves, and its first members were the harbour pilots who knew every smuggler's cove.

wander: something comes in with the tide
smugglers unloading in the dark
claws clicking on the rocks
trap: a wrecker's tripline on the cliff path
a sea-cave gate that drops with the tide
hazard: the tide races in through the cave
a storm breaks over the cliffs
puzzle: a lighthouse lens that must be turned to open the vault
parley: a smuggler who will sell out his captain
a merfolk scout with a grievance
treasure: a smugglers' cache in the sea-cave
a wrecked galleon's strongroom
boss: the master of the drowned deck
the thing the wreckers serve

themes.name: frozen north
themes.text: ice fields under the aurora, whale-bone camps and frozen lakes
history: The Stonekings ruled the ice before the frost giant clans, and the frost-sworn jarls drove the giants into the glaciers and never knelt to Caldor.
Caldor sent three armies into this ice, and the frost-sworn jarls sent every one of them home in boxes.
The frost giants of the Rime Clans still sleep in the glaciers, and the jarls do not dig.

names: the Wreck of the Pale Gull

wander: howling on the wind
white shapes against the white snow
trap: thin ice over black water
hazard: a whiteout that freezes the unready
an ice bridge that groans and cracks
puzzle: runes on a frozen door that thaw only in order
parley: a frost-sworn hunter who honours guests
a giant who wants a contest, not a fight
treasure: a jarl's hoard sealed in the ice
furs and amber in a dead trader's sled
boss: whatever holds the ice hall
the thing under the glacier

themes.name: desert
themes.text: dunes, salt flats and buried cities under a cruel sun
history: Under these sands lies the green river land of the Ninefold Throne of Ashkaar, which lost its rain to the Stormmother.
The nine masked kings of Ashkaar are buried under these dunes, each in a tomb grander than the last.
The ninth mask-queen of Ashkaar tried to bind the Stormmother, and the rain has not fallen here since.

names: the Tomb of the Nine Masks

wander: something moves under the sand
riders on the dune crest
the dust-devil is not wind
trap: a sand-filled pit under the tomb door
a dart trap in the false burial chamber
hazard: a day without water
a sandstorm that strips the skin
puzzle: a sphinx's question at the gate
a star-chart lock on the inner tomb
parley: a nomad who trades water for news
a djinn-blooded merchant with a map
treasure: a god-king's grave goods
a caravan's lost gold
boss: the guardian of the god-king's tomb
the master of the buried city

themes.name: volcanic wastes
themes.text: lava fields, obsidian spires and sulphur springs
history: Vermithrax the Old Wyrm sleeps in chains under this smoking mountain, where the Smith-King forged them and died.
Dwarves and elves fought side by side here to chain Vermithrax, the only time they ever have.
The obsidian here is the Stonekings' halls, melted when the Old Wyrm burned them.

wander: heat-shimmer that walks
something swims in the lava
trap: a vent rigged to blow scalding steam
hazard: a lava tube that floods with fire
choking sulphur fumes
puzzle: a forge-lock that opens only to the right heat
parley: an azer smith who wants his anvil back
treasure: masterwork arms cooling in a forgotten forge
boss: the master of the furnace
the thing in the caldera

themes.name: fey crossing
themes.text: twilight glades and mirrored lakes where the seasons run out of order
history: Here the Court of First Leaves withdrew into twilight, and its hags and lords still keep the bargains it broke long ago.
The Lord of the Last Door is said to keep a house in these glades, and to sell what no one else will.
The seasons here run in the order they ran when the Court of First Leaves held the whole world.

wander: laughter in the leaves that is not kind
a hunting horn from nowhere
trap: a fairy ring that steals a year
hazard: a path that loops back on itself for a day
a feast nobody should eat
puzzle: a bargain worded to trap the careless
a mirror that shows the way only to the honest
parley: a satyr who will guide for a song
a pixie who trades names
treasure: a fey lord's gifts, half of them real
gold that has not yet turned to leaves
boss: the court's cruel champion
whatever rules the hollow hill

themes.name: drowned empire
themes.text: drowned towers, coral streets and tide pools over Caldor's sunken harbour wards
history: When the sea rose over the Coil's temples it took a whole quarter of Caldor's coast with them; the bells still ring at low tide.
Free Port salvagers dive the drowned streets for the Ford-Kings' customs gold, and not all of them come up.
Something old moved into the sunken counting-houses and taught the fish to keep accounts.

names: the Bell Tower Under the Waves

wander: something vast moves under the hull of the wreck
drowned sailors who still man their stations
trap: a sluice gate rigged to flood the hall
hazard: the tide turns and the corridors fill
a rip that drags them toward the deep
puzzle: a tide-clock that opens the vault at one hour only
parley: a merrow queen who wants her crown back from the deep
treasure: Caldor's customs gold, barnacled in its chests
boss: the thing that keeps the drowned accounts
the master of the sunken harbour

themes.name: titans' battlefield
themes.text: a plain of giant bones, rusted siege engines the size of towers and craters where Stonekings fell
history: Here the last Stonekings stood against Vermithrax's brood; their ribs still arch over the grass like the vaults of a hall.
The dwarves of the Smith-King's Holds walked here once to count the giant dead and gave up after three years.
Shepherds swear the bones shift between seasons, as if the fallen were still trying to stand.

wander: scavengers picking the marrow out of a giant's femur
the ground heaves as something tunnels under the bones
trap: a rusted ballista still wound and waiting
hazard: a rib the size of a bridge gives way underfoot
puzzle: a giant's war-horn that wakes the field if sounded wrong
parley: a giant ghost who wants to know who won
treasure: a Stoneking's arm-ring big enough to sit in
boss: what nests in the titan's skull
the last of the field's dead to keep fighting

themes.name: storm coast
themes.text: sea cliffs under endless storms, lightning-struck towers and eyries of things that ride the wind
history: The Stormmother poured the seas here first, and here she still comes to rage.
Free Port captains will not round these headlands in autumn; the ones who did are carved on the cliff as a warning.
Cloud giants keep castles in the thunderheads and come down to the cliffs to trade lightning for iron.

wander: shapes in the thunderheads that dive
wreckers on the cliff path with lanterns
trap: a false lighthouse lamp that lures ships, and climbers, onto the rocks
hazard: a lightning strike on the iron stair
a gale that tears them off the ledge
puzzle: storm-bells that must be rung with the thunder
parley: a cloud giant who trades only for stories
treasure: a storm-glass that holds a living squall
boss: the lord of the eyrie
what rides the eye of the storm

themes.name: god-king's remains
themes.text: the shattered colossus of the Ninth god-king, his mask a mountain and his tomb-city in its shadow
history: The Ninth of Ashkaar's masked god-kings had himself carved as a colossus to look the Stormmother in the eye; she broke it when she took the rain.
His priests still serve in the colossus's hollow skull, waiting for a king who says he is only sleeping.
The templars burn every relic carried out of here, and still some reach the oasis markets.

names: the Stair That Climbs Too Far

wander: masked priests who walk in step and never blink
sand that pours upward into the colossus's eye
trap: a weighing-scale floor that tips the unworthy into the pit
hazard: the sun through the god-king's eye-glass, focused into a beam
puzzle: nine masks that must be hung in the order of the kings
parley: the god-king's last vizier, who has not died yet
treasure: a gilded death mask of the Ninth
boss: the god-king's undying guardian
the one who wears the Ninth's mask now

themes.name: infernal breach
themes.text: a wound in the world below the Chained Mountain, where brimstone rains and devils hold court
history: When the Smith-King died at his furnace forging Vermithrax's chains, the heat of it burned through the floor of the world.
Devils came up through the burn to bargain with the sleeping wyrm; the templars have kept a siege line round it for a thousand years.
Every pact signed here is filed somewhere below, and the clerks below never lose one.

wander: a legion of devils marching in perfect step
demons fighting over a scrap of a soul
trap: a contract inked on the floor that binds whoever steps on it
hazard: brimstone rain
a river of fire that changes its course
puzzle: a lock of nine seals, each sworn to a different devil
parley: an imp clerk who will sell the citadel's plans, for a price
treasure: a devil's ledger of the souls it holds
boss: the duke of the breach
what clawed its way up from the pit

themes.name: spellscar
themes.text: glassed earth and floating stones where Caldor's last court-mages tore the sky trying to hold back the Long Night
history: When Caldor's last king would not cross the Ferryman's river, his court-mages tried to hold the Long Night back by force, and tore the sky here.
The stones still float where the spell left them, and time runs crooked in the hollows.
Gnome surveyors map the Scar every year and never draw the same map twice.

wander: constructs still running a spell nobody remembers
echoes of the court-mages, casting the same spell forever
trap: a warding circle that turns spells back on their casters
hazard: a hollow where time runs a year an hour
wild magic that turns the air to glass
puzzle: a spell left half-cast, waiting for its last word
parley: a court-mage who has been dying for twelve hundred years
treasure: a court-mage's spellbook, still warm
boss: the archmage who would not stop
the thing the spell let in

isles._doc: Floating isles (World.PlaceIsles): far sites in high country torn loose and drifting above the clouds. Only a company that can fly, or rides the sky dock's airship, gets there.

ruins._doc: Old works near the town fallen to ruin (Systems/Ruins.cs): a lair like any other until cleared, then restored for 'cost' gold to serve for good. {A} a word of the country, {B} a name.

kinds.gives: brings clean water down to the wells again, and the townsfolk are happier for it
kinds.text: Masons and well-diggers set the old arches of {site} running again. Clean water comes down to the town's wells.

kinds.gives: guards the road in, and the town's defence rises
kinds.text: The council puts doors back on {site} and a watch in its towers. Nothing comes up the road unseen.

kinds.gives: keeps watch over the hills, and raiders are seen half a day sooner
kinds.text: A lamp burns again at the top of {site}. Its watchers will see raiders coming half a day sooner.

kinds.gives: stands as a bastion before the town, and the town's defence rises
kinds.text: Ivy comes down off the bastions of {site}, and guns and a garrison go up. The old star fort guards the town again.

kinds.gives: gives a timber lookout over the passes, and a little warning and defence
kinds.text: Carpenters roof {site} in fresh timber and a lookout climbs to the top. It watches the passes for the town.
